newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down 7 to 818 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down 7 to 818 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 818 as of Jan. 17, down seven from the prior week and 102 above the year-ago total of 716, Baker Hughes Inc reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by four to 685, while rigs working offshore fell one to 110. The number of rigs active in inland waters was down two to 23.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Texas, which was down 20, Oklahoma, which has up 13 and New Mexico, which was up six.

A total of 335 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down 11 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas was up five at 482, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects was down one at one.
In Canada, the number of working rigs was unchanged at 410 vs. 367 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 162 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Jan. 17, up two from a week ago,
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 183, was 88.5 percent.
The number of working rigs in the European/Mediterranean area dropped one this week to 105 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 106, a utilization rate of 99.1 pct.
The worldwide rig count remained the same at 557 out of a total fleet of 606, making the utilization rate 91.9 percent.
